title: Faye screen protocol v1
description: Contract between the Faye server and the Login UI. GET /api/flows/{flowId} returns a ScreenResponse; POST /api/flows/{flowId}/submit takes a SubmitRequest and returns a ScreenResponse, a RedirectResponse (the host redirects the browser) or a HandoffResponse (the host hands the result to the page that embeds the Login UI). Failures return an ErrorResponse. Both calls need the cookie faye_flow_{flowId} that Faye set when the flow started; without its value the flow is answered as unknown (404, flow_not_found). The root schema accepts any response.

nonce.description: Echo in the next SubmitRequest; single use.

step.description: Innermost enclosing step id, when there is one.

path.description: Where the Login UI shows this screen, with ?flow={flowId} (ADR 0029). A label only: the flow decides the screen, so a browser at another path is shown this screen and moved to this path.

Branding.description: How the tenant dresses its login screens, when it sets any of it: appearance and two optional controls (ADR 0033). The layout is not tenant configurable.

name.description: Shown above every screen, and in the footer of every screen.

showPassword.description: Password fields have a button that shows what was typed.

signUp.description: The identifier screen shows a sign up button. Sign up is not supported yet: the button says so.

code.description: Why the flow came back to this screen, e.g. invalid_credentials, invalid_code. Copy lives in the Login UI.

errors.description: Failures that sent the flow back to this screen.

attemptsLeft.description: Attempts left after the failure in errors.

passkey.description: Present when passkey autofill (WebAuthn conditional mediation) is offered. Offered to every account alike.

password.description: Present when the screen asks for the password with the identifier: answer with IdentifierPasswordPayload. Never offered with passkey.

remember.description: Present when the tenant offers "keep me signed in": the answer may carry remember (ADR 0033).

identifier.description: The identifier being signed in, shown as an editable chip.

options.description: Option ids of the enabled choose options, in flow order. Labels live in the Login UI.

register.description: Present when creating a passkey rather than using one. The user may skip unless required is set.

algorithms.description: COSE algorithm ids the server verifies, in order of preference.

required.description: With register: the step requires a passkey, so the user may not skip (ADR 0038); absent when they may.

secret.description: base32 TOTP secret, for manual entry.

uri.description: otpauth:// URI, shown as a QR code.

CodeSentScreen.description: A one time code Faye sent by email or text message (ADR 0032). Answered with a CodePayload; the resend action sends another. The code itself is never in the screen.

resendIn.description: Seconds until the resend action may send another code; absent when no more may be sent.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the last code sent expires.

PhoneEnrollScreen.description: Adds a phone number for the signed in person (ADR 0032): the send action, with a PhonePayload, texts a code to it; the screen then shows to and expiresIn and is answered with a CodePayload, or with a SkipPayload unless required (ADR 0038).

to.description: The number the last code went to, masked; absent until one was sent.

resendIn.description: Seconds until the send action may send another code; absent when none was sent yet or no more may be sent.

expiresIn.description: Seconds until the last code sent expires; absent until one was sent.

required.description: The step requires a phone, so the person may not skip (ADR 0038); absent when they may.

QrScreen.description: QR code sign in, on the device signing in (ADR 0032): draw url as a QR code and show number; send the poll action every 2 seconds, and once status is approved, expired or refused, answer with an empty payload (ContinuePayload).

url.description: What the QR code encodes: the Login UI's /approve/{token}.

number.description: Shown beside the QR code; the person picks it on the phone.

status.description: As the last poll read it.

QrApproveScreen.description: QR code sign in, on the phone (ADR 0032): approves the waiting device once the person picks the number it shows. Answered with a NumberPayload; a wrong number refuses the sign in.

device.description: The waiting device's browser, e.g. Chrome on macOS.

code.description: Safe error code; copy lives in the Login UI.

PollRequest.description: A screen action (ADR 0032): qr reads whether its QR code was approved.

ResendRequest.description: A screen action, not an answer (ADR 0032): code_sent sends another code. It runs no handler and spends no attempt; the response is the same screen, with errors [send_limited] when a limit refused it. An action the screen does not take is refused (400, unknown_action).

SendRequest.description: A screen action (ADR 0032): phone_enroll texts a code to the number typed.

NumberPayload.description: Answers qr_approve: the number the waiting device shows.

remember.description: Answers identifier when it offers remember: whether the person asked to stay signed in on this browser (ADR 0033).

IdentifierPasswordPayload.description: Answers identifier when it asks for the password.

remember.description: Answers identifier when it offers remember: whether the person asked to stay signed in on this browser (ADR 0033).

PasskeyPayload.description: Answers passkey, or identifier when it offers autofill.

passkey.description: The browser's PublicKeyCredential as JSON (base64url fields).

remember.description: Answers identifier when it offers remember: whether the person asked to stay signed in on this browser (ADR 0033).

SkipPayload.description: Declines creating a passkey (passkey screen with register), or adding a phone (phone_enroll); refused when the screen is required.

ContinuePayload.description: Answers error, and qr once its poll read where the QR code is.

redirectTo.description: Where the browser goes next: always an absolute http or https URL, so the Login UI can hand it to window.location (ADR 0007).

failed.description: Present, and true, only when the sign in failed: the host has been told, and the Login UI shows /error?reason=failed instead of following redirectTo (ADR 0031). Never set for a consent the person denied, which goes back to the app.

HandoffResponse.description: A finished flow whose host does not redirect: result is the host's own (for example a one time code its system exchanges server to server for the outcome), handed to the page that embeds the Login UI.
